[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Full Fine-Tuning vs Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) in NLP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Adapting massive pre-trained language models to downstream NLP tasks is a core workflow in modern machine learning. Two primary paradigms dominate this space: Full Fine-Tuning and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT). This tutorial explores the architectural differences, resource implications, and practical implementation details of both approaches."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Full Fine-Tuning"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In Full Fine-Tuning, every parameter in the pre-trained neural network is updated during backpropagation. While this allows the model to adapt deeply to the nuances of the target dataset, it comes with massive computational overhead."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Updates 100% of the model parameters, requiring massive GPU VRAM to store gradients, optimizer states (like AdamW), and activations."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prone to catastrophic forgetting if the downstream dataset is small and vastly different from the pre-training corpus."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Requires storing a distinct, full-sized copy of the model weights for every single downstream task."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Understanding Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"PEFT methods freeze the vast majority of the pre-trained model weights and only train a small subset of parameters (often less than 1 percent). This drastically reduces memory footprints while maintaining competitive performance against full fine-tuning."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into the attention layers of the transformer."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Drastically lowers memory requirements, allowing engineers to fine-tune large models on consumer-grade hardware."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enables modular deployment where a single base model can be paired with multiple tiny task-specific adapters."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Practical Implementation: LoRA with Hugging Face PEFT"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following Python code snippet demonstrates how to configure and apply LoRA using the Hugging Face transformers and peft libraries."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainingArguments, Trainer
from peft import get_peft_model, LoraConfig, TaskType

model_id = "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf"
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, load_in_8bit=True, device_map="auto")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)

peft_config = LoraConfig(
    task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM,
    inference_mode=False,
    r=8,
    lora_alpha=32,
    lora_dropout=0.1
)

model = get_peft_model(model, peft_config)
model.print_trainable_parameters()"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Full Fine-Tuning remains useful when maximum task adaptation is needed and compute resources are unbounded, PEFT has become the industry standard for NLP due to its efficiency, speed, and drastically reduced storage costs."}]
